chapter: Touring, recording and Fletcher's band in the 1940s
title: Where his 78s and original arrangements are kept
summary: Horace's sister keeps some 78s in Georgia, 500 more are with friends in Minneapolis, and he has original arrangements in his basement.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Do you have any of these recordings, any of these 78's?
I don't have them. My sister has them in Georgia. She's quite a storage person, you know.
Are they pretty well preserved? I mean --
She has taken care of them?

She takes things. Very good care of them. Plus I left 500 78's with very good friends of ours in Minneapolis, Minnesota, which we intend this summer, the first week we're off, take off. We're gonna go and get those.
And we hope they still have them.
Well, we keep in touch with each other. Every now and then my wife mentions about them, 'Say, we're gonna come get our records one day.' I hope they are still there.
Do you have some of these arrangements in the arrangements that you have?
